articles.title: What Is Host Header Injection? Detection to Exploitation with Burp
articles.excerpt: There's a small line inside every HTTP request: the "Host" header. When your browser goes to a site, it tells the server "this is where I've come." Since hundreds of sites can live on a single server,…
articles.body: There's a small line inside every HTTP request: the "Host" header. When your browser goes to a site, it tells the server "this is where I've come." Since hundreds of sites can live on a single server, the server figures out which one you want from this line. But some applications trust this header too much. The Host header is entirely under the user's control. If you want, you write your own domain there, and the server takes it as correct and uses it. That's exactly where Host Header Injection begins. So where does the application get into danger when it uses this header? The most classic spot is password reset . You forgot your password, so you click "reset my password." The server sends you an email with a link in it. Where does it get that link's domain from?
articles.author: Emin ÜZÜN

articles.title: What Is Hashcat? Installation and Basic Usage
articles.excerpt: Hashcat is a password cracking tool. Systems don't store passwords as plain text. When you type "password", the system first runs it through a hash function. MD5, SHA-256, bcrypt. pentests and CTF sol…
articles.body: Hashcat is a password cracking tool. If you have a hash value and want to find the password, it's one of the tools you turn to. Systems don't store passwords as plain text. When you type "password", the system first runs it through a hash function. Like MD5, SHA-256, bcrypt . The resulting value is always the same, but reversing it is extremely hard computationally. Hashcat doesn't actually try to reverse it. It hashes every word in your wordlist and compares it with your value. In other words, it tries to find a match. It's a tool people often turn to in pentests and CTF solutions. Installation If you're on Linux: sudo apt update && sudo apt install hashcat For Windows , you can download the zip from hashcat.net and extract it. Keep your GPU drivers up to date.
articles.author: Emin ÜZÜN

articles.title: Kubernetes Container Runtime Internals: Understanding How containerd and CRI-O Work Behind the Scenes
articles.excerpt: When a Pod starts in Kubernetes, several components work together behind the scenes to get its containers up and running. One of the first components involved in this process is the container runtime.…
articles.body: When a Pod starts in Kubernetes, several components work together behind the scenes to get its containers up and running. One of the first components involved in this process is the container runtime. The container runtime is responsible for preparing the container environment, setting up isolation, and starting the application process. It acts as the bridge between Kubernetes and the underlying operating system, ensuring that containers run as expected. Understanding how container runtimes work helps explain what happens behind the scenes when Kubernetes schedules and starts a Pod. What Is a Container Runtime? A container runtime is a system-level component responsible for managing the execution and lifecycle of containers on a Kubernetes worker node.

The 191-foot-tall (58 meters) rocket was transferred 0.93 miles (1.5 kilometers) from a vertical integration building to the pad over the course of around two hours, starting around 4 a.m. EST (0900 GMT, or 5 p.m. Beijing Time), according to China Central Television (CCTV). articles.title: Don't miss Saturn shine close to the moon on Nov. 20
articles.excerpt: The moon shines with Saturn in the constellation Pisces after sunset on Nov. 20
articles.body: The moon shines close to the ringed giant Saturn after sunset on Nov. 20, presenting a spectacular naked-eye display as the stars of the Great Square of Pegasus twinkle nearby. Saturn's steady light will appear a little over 5 degrees from the 82%-lit moon in the southeastern sky after the sun dips below the horizon for viewers in the U.S. — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length. Moonlight will hide fainter stars from view, though you should be able to spot Algenib, Markab, Alpheratz and Scheat arrayed in a diamond formation above the lunar disk, marking out the asterism of the Great Square of Pegasus in the November sky.
